parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction: no trans-specific traveler-facing exposure is documented on any axis. The male-only sodomy statute is a dead letter — no prosecutions ever reported — and thus a secondary, tangential signal under the rubric, not a dominant one. Documented positives: a locally recognised third-gender role (Pinapinaaine/Binabinaaine), a 2015 report of no societal SO-based discrimination or violence, a named employment-discrimination ground, and a 2016 UN vote against defunding the SOGI Independent Expert — institutional-culture signals of non-hostility. The present-tense record stops in 2016; absence of evidence is not safety, and no entry-screening, document, custody, or care evidence exists for visitors. Extrapolating from an unenforced statute, embedded gender-diverse tradition, and no documented targeting yields a Reduced Risk score, held below the acceptance-with-protections tier only by the open questions.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No evidence on marker recognition, screening, or document mismatch handling for visitors.
entry_documents.protection: No documented border friction either; statute is unenforced.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown how home passports with markers would be handled at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sections 153-155 carry 5-14 year penalties but no prosecution ever reported; custody rules for trans detainees undocumented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented; but dead-letter statute implies no custodial pipeline.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If ever charged, remedies are thin — no SOGI constitutional protection.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility, bathroom, or ward rules sourced.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. Gender-affirming care access for visitors unsourced.
care_services.protection: Employment Code Art. 107(2)(b) covers sexual orientation — resident-facing climate signal only.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Unenforced morality statute on the books; no police targeting documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2016 UN vote retaining SOGI Expert mandate signals official non-hostility; no UPR pushback on decriminalisation but no enforcement either.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Government considered SOGI anti-discrimination legislation (2015), outcome unknown.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No rules on travelling families or minors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2015 report: no societal SO-based discrimination or violence; a decade stale. Traditional third-gender role suggests presentation is legible, not threatened.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Embedded cultural category (Pinapinaaine) is a documented acceptance signal.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI anti-discrimination protection outside employment; constitution omits both grounds; post-2016 status of statute and social climate unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Employment Code ground since 2015; anti-discrimination bill under consideration.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions are unresolved, not exposures; they cap the score but lightly.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far safer than 0.35-A: no universal-exposure measure, no register, no visitor-specific enforcement. The statute here is a documented dead letter, not an operating exclusion mechanism.
Safer than 0.55-B: no documented secondary screening, denial of entry, or administrative friction against trans visitors; 0.55-B's border exposure exceeds anything in this dossier.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor documents working remedies, trained officers, and a functioning tribunal. Here no operative protection is documented and the present record is thin and dated, capping the score in the lower Reduced Risk band.
Comparable to 0.65-A: no imprisonment threat, no lethal pathway, broadly non-hostile society; but this jurisdiction documents less working recourse, so it sits slightly below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a national statute book with an unenforced, sexuality-targeted criminal provision, no documented visitor-facing restriction on any axis, a locally recognised gender-diverse tradition, and weak but non-hostile institutional culture (UN vote, employment ground, pending anti-discrimination consideration). No exposure tier from the precedence ladder is documented: the worst feature is a latent tangential statute plus unanswered questions about present law and visitor treatment. Under the thin-data extrapolation rule, structural signals — dead-letter statute, embedded acceptance, no record of relief or enforcement — resolve riskily downward from the acceptance tier but well clear of any universal-exposure or targeting tier. Score: 0.62, with the deduction carried mainly by the unverified present status of law and climate, not by any documented exposure.
